label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
To: timeline
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Draft — not for posting yet

Spent the last two Saturdays redoing the electric in a buddy’s shed. Been doing this 26 years and I still open things up that make me stand there with my hands on my hips like somebody’s disappointed father.

This one had a little of everything.

Power came from THREE orange extension cords plugged into each other, out a basement window, across the yard and under the deck. Apparently the plan was to keep adding cord until electricity got tired and stopped arguing.

Found a splice wrapped in duct tape. Not electrical tape. Duct tape. Great for holding your busted lawn chair together. Not what I want standing between your wiring and a fire.

There was a 30 amp breaker feeding 14 gauge wire. That breaker was letting the wire get into trouble long before it was going to step in.

Shed outlet wired with speaker wire. I guess if the lights don’t work you can at least hear the fire in stereo.

My personal favorite: a regular outlet with a GFCI STICKER on it.

A sticker.

Well hell, put a “paid off” sticker on my truck while you’re at it. See if the bank goes along.

Ceiling fan box held up by one drywall screw. One. That screw had more responsibility than some foremen I’ve worked for.

Mouse nest in the junction box. Mice were fine. Completely unbothered. Only occupants on the property who apparently thought the electric was acceptable.

Then I open the panel and inside the door, in Sharpie:

“SHED - DONT TOUCH - RON”

Buddy’s wife is standing there and goes, “Who’s Ron?”

Like I’d know. Lady, I just got here. All I know about Ron is he didn’t want a second opinion.

Now before everybody starts, I don’t think whoever did this was evil. Cheap and a little proud, probably. That’s most of these jobs. Somebody gets something to turn on and figures that means they did it right.

It does not.

An outlet can work and still be dangerous. A fan can spin while it’s getting ready to come down. A breaker that doesn’t trip isn’t proof everything’s fine, especially when it’s too big for the wire it’s supposed to protect.

We got the mess out and redid it with proper wiring, real GFCI protection, proper boxes and outlets, and a fan support that doesn’t depend on one screw having a good day.

I’m laughing about what we found because otherwise I’d still be standing in that yard swearing. But this stuff starts fires. It burns sheds down, and it can take the house and people with it.

Call a licensed electrician. Not your buddy whose qualifications are a YouTube video and “I’ve done a bunch of these.”

You can be a good guy and still wire something that’ll kill somebody. Knowing when to call somebody is nothing to be embarrassed about.
